rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: For verbs of five or more letters, forms such as أغزيت and غازيت use yāʾ for wāw: the imperfect loses wāw under kasra and has already shifted to yāʾ.
rows.anchor: سألت الخليل عن ذلك فقال إنما قلبت ياء لأنك إذا قلت يفعل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: In تغازينا and ترجينا, alif substitutes for the yāʾ that replaced wāw; the tāʾ is added to غازيت and رجيت.
rows.anchor: قال الألف بدل من الياء ههنا التي أبدلت مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ضوضيت and قوقيت, reduplicating a pair works like repeating one consonant: the doubled wāws parallel the doubled yāʾ of حييت and wāws of قوة.
rows.anchor: وقال ضوضيت وقوقيت بمنزلة ضعضعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as حاحيت and عاعيت likewise repeat two consonants; alif is substituted for yāʾ because of their resemblance, as forms like الحيحاء and العيعاء show.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حاحيت وعاعيت وهاهيت ولكنهم أبدلوا الألف لشبهها بالياء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: دهديت الجعل is analyzed as دهدهت: yāʾ replaces hāʾ because the letters resemble one another in lightness and unobtrusiveness.
rows.anchor: فيما زعم الخليل دهدهت بمنزلة دحرجة ولكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غوغاء has two analyses: feminine, uninflected like عوراء, or masculine and declinable, with doubled root consonants like قمقام.
rows.anchor: فأما الغوغاء ففيها قولان أما من قال غوغاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the masculine analysis, غوغاء is declinable like قمقام; other reduplicated forms are analogized to this type or to three-letter reduplication such as غصص and غصة.
rows.anchor: وأما من قال غوغاء فذكر وصرف فإنما هي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In موماة, like دوداة and مرمر, the first mīm is part of the root; this common pattern is unlike تمسكن, since an extra initial mīm is rare here.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة الدوداة والمرمر ولا تجعلها بمنزلة تمسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif in فيفاة is extra because الفيّف is also used with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وأما قولهم الفيفاة فالألف زائدة لأنهم يقولون الفيف في هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قيقاء and زيزاء follow علباء, since a form like قلقال occurs only as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وأما القيقاء والزيزاء فبمنزلة العلباء لأنه لا يكون في الكلام مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An added yāʾ in fourth position behaves like a root consonant, so سلقيت and جعبيت follow ضوضيت and قوقيت.
rows.anchor: وإذا كانت الياء زائدة رابعة فهي تجري مجرى ما هو من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المروراة follows الشجوجاة and صمحمح, rather than عثوثل, because the صمحمح pattern is more common.
rows.anchor: وأما المروراة فبمنزلة الشجوجاة وهما بمنزلة صمحمح ولا تجعلهما على عثوثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قيقاءة and زيزاءة are singular forms of قيقاء and زيزاء; some also say قيقاءة وقواق, treating yāʾ as a substitute as in قيل.
rows.anchor: فإنما أرادوا الواحد على القيقاء والزيزاء وقد قال بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أثفية is فعليّة for speakers who say أثفت, but أفعولة for those who say ثفيت.
rows.anchor: وسألته عن أثفية فقال هي فعلية فيمن قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With لعل, ليت, رويد, عليك, هلم and similar particles, attached object pronouns behave as with verbs, but are weaker: عليكه and رويده are possible while detached إياه is not normally used.
rows.anchor: فعلامات الإضمار حالهن هاهنا كحالهن في الفعل لا تقوى أن تقول عليك إياه

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus heard some Arabs say عليكني spontaneously; others avoid نى and نا here because عليك بي and عليك بنا suffice.
rows.anchor: وحدثنا يونس أنه سمع [ من العرب ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Detached إياك is awkward after رأيت when the clitic already expresses the same object; this economy also explains why comparable forms after إن and ضرب زيد are rejected.
rows.anchor: قبيح أن تقول رأيت فيها إياك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exceptive clauses such as ما أتاني إلا أنت and ما رأيت إلا إياك are different: moving إلا makes the statement impossible, while deleting it reverses the meaning.
rows.anchor: أنت وما رأيت إلا إياك فإنه لا يدخل على هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A definite noun can replace an indefinite one to identify it, as in مررت برجل عبد الله; the Quranic صراط مستقيم صراط الله gives the same construction.
rows.anchor: إنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم صراط الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After مررت بقوم, coordinated definite names may stand in apposition; nominative is strong because it leaves the intended meaning intact.
rows.anchor: أيضا مررت بقوم عبد الله وزيد وخالد والرفع جيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A definite noun can replace another definite noun either to correct a mistaken first name or to shift the intended reference to the second.
rows.anchor: التي تكون بدلا من المعرفة فهو كقولك مررت بعبد الله زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase after an initial statement can be a new predicate answering an implied question: مهلهل's أخوالنا وهم بنو الأعمام and مررت بعبد الله أخوك illustrate it.
rows.anchor: مررت بعبد الله أخوك كأنه قيل له من هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأسد شدة after رجل can raise his status as an appositive or restart as an answer to ما هو; it is not an adjective, since definite and indefinite nouns cannot modify one another.
rows.anchor: كأنك قلت مررت برجل كامل لأنك أردت أن ترفع شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Independent predication is especially strong in partitive clarification; the usage أخوالنا is good Arabic and has a parallel in an indefinite description.
rows.anchor: وهذا عربي جيد قوله أخوالنا وقد جاء في النكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feminine tāʾ can compensate for a deleted final weak letter in verbal nouns, as in إقامة, استعانة and إراءة; the verse has إقامة الصلاة and إيتاء الزكاة.
rows.anchor: لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the full form is retained, compensation may be omitted: اختيار has no feminine tāʾ, and إراءة also occurs as إراء, parallel to إقاما.
rows.anchor: وقالوا اخترت اختيارا فلم يلحقوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deletion is unavailable in تعزية and similar forms; تجزئة and تهنئة retain their forms by analogy with derived forms, just as أرأيت was reshaped as أريت after أقمت.
rows.anchor: وأما عزيت تعزية ونحوها فلا يجوز الحذف فيه

rows.speaker: يونس والخليل
rows.claim: In مالي إلا زيدا صديق وعمرا, accusative continues the first construction; nominative makes the added name a new clause, as in وعمرو لي. Yūnus and al-Khalīl endorse both parses.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول يونس والخليل رحمهما الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second exception cannot be nominative apposition to an already excepted item, as in ما أتاني إلا زيد إلا عمرا; alternatively, one exception may be accusative and the other nominative.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز الرفع في عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ما أتاني إلا عمرا إلا بشرا أحد, بشر substitutes for أحد and is moved forward; the poet al-Kumayt's فما لي إلا الله غيرك ناصر supports treating غيرك like an exceptive.
rows.anchor: فما لي إلا الله لا رب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hāritha's verse, غير means مثل rather than an exception: only breaths remain like the corpses; a Medina-house verse is likewise read with غير as adjective or exception.
rows.anchor: يا كعب صبرا على ما كان من حدث

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: For the Medina-house line, treating غير as an adjective permits nominative دار الخليفة; treating it as an exception requires one of the two nouns to be accusative, Ibn Abī Isḥāq's analysis.
rows.anchor: ومن جعلها بمنزلة الاستثناء لم يكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating إلا زيد إلا أبو عبد الله is good when both names identify the same person, as emphatic repetition; it may also be a correction after a slip, with a poetic clarification as evidence.
rows.anchor: إذا أردت أن تبين وتوضح قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vocative truncation can drop jointly added final letters: عثمان becomes عثم, مروان مرو, and أسماء أسم; poets provide matching examples.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك في عثمان يا عثم أقبل وفي مروان يا مرو أقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paired suffixes are removed together when they were added together, as with مسلمان; a name like بنون loses only نون, since names cannot be shorter than three letters, and the remainder may be treated as an unaugmented name.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ترخيم رجل يقال له مسلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When echoing a noun with أي in a question, match its number and gender: رجل gives أيا, رجلين أَيَين, امرأة أية, امرأتين أيتين, and نسوة أيات.
rows.anchor: قال رأيت رجلا قلت أيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative form follows the case of the noun in the preceding statement, because the question echoes the speaker's grammatical construction.
rows.anchor: على ما وضع عليه المتكلم كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a proper name, use من عبد الله rather than أيا; أي عبد الله is nominative and cannot echo case as من عبد الله can, because من is being used outside its usual construction.
rows.anchor: إذا قال رأيت عبد الله قلت أي عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In exclamations such as ويحه رجلا, ولله دره رجلا and حسبك به رجلا, من may be added for emphasis; رجل is accusative, governed by the first construction and outside its initial wording.
rows.anchor: وانتصب الرجل لأنه ليس من الكلام الأول وعمل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويحه expresses admiration without specifying its aspect; adding فارسا or حافظا identifies the quality being praised.
rows.anchor: فارسا وحافظا فقد اختصصت ولم تبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عباس بن مرداس's أبرحت فارسا means roughly كفى بك فارسا; the bāʾ reinforces the construction. Al-Aʿshā's أبرحت ربا وأبرحت جارا and أكرم به رجلا are parallel.
rows.anchor: ومرة يحميهم إذا ما تمددوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In nisba formation from a name of at least four letters ending in yāʾ after kasra, the old yāʾ is deleted before the suffixal yāʾ, avoiding two adjacent sukūns; examples include ناجي, أدلي, صحاري and ثماني.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان الاسم في هذه الصفة أذهبت الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as يماني and بخاتي reflect deletion of the two yāʾs introduced by nisba; يرمي remains يرمي, while عرقوة yields عرقي.
rows.anchor: رجل اسمه بخاتي لقلت هذا بخاتي كما ترى

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl says a dialect that opens the preceding kasra in يثربي or تغلبي is altering the form; by the same pattern, يرمي would yield يرموي. The poet's الحانوي contrasts with expected الحاني.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل من قال في يثرب

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl treats فتح in تغلبي as optional alteration like سهلي and بصري, not a required nisba rule; otherwise forms such as يشكري and جلهمي would be expected. Yūnus agrees.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل الذين قالوا تغلبي ففتحوا مغيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In vocative use, names of three or more letters ending in feminine hāʾ usually drop it, whether proper names or common nouns; shorter examples include شاة and ثبة.
rows.anchor: فأما ما كان اسما غالبا فنحو قولك يا سلم أقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs retain feminine hāʾ in the vocative, saying يا سلمة; even speakers who delete it in connected speech restore it at pause to show the final consonant's vowel.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ناسا من العرب يثبتون الهاء فيقولون يا سلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At pause, hāʾ is retained in forms like يا سلمة and ارمه to avoid leaving the deleted consonant unvocalized; poetic meter can license its omission because rhyme length replaces it.
rows.anchor: إذا وقفوا قالوا يا سلمة ويا طلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vocative hāʾ is more readily deleted than other letters because it has no replacement in this position, whereas it becomes tāʾ elsewhere; a reliable Arab said يا حرمل for يا حرمله.
rows.anchor: يا حرمل يريد يا حرمله كما قال بعضهم إرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feminine hāʾ does not license deleting preceding added letters that would otherwise remain; examples include طائفية to يا طائفي and مرجانة to يا مرجان, with analogous treatment of root letters.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هاء التأنيث إذا كانت بعد حرف زائد لو لم تكن بعده حذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا, like رب, cannot govern a definite noun; treating ولا العباس as governed by لا would require the same construction with رب, and لا غلام لك وأخوه illustrates the contrast.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يجوز للا أن تعمل في معرفة كما لا يجوز ذلك لرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the pattern كل شاة وسخلتها بدرهم, coordination after لا رجل لك takes accusative وأخاه, understood as لا رجل لك وأخا له.
rows.anchor: فأما من قال كل شاة وسخلتها بدرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisba forms from two-radical nouns restore the lost final root consonant, as in أبوي, أخوي and حموي; dual and plural forms expose that root, so restoration is stronger in nisba.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك في أب أبوي وفي أخ أخوي وفي حم حموي ولا يجوز إلا ذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers treat هن like أب, saying هنوان and هنوات, then derive هنوي; سنة likewise has the regular سنوي, while an hāʾ-root analysis gives سنيهة and سانهت, like شفة.
rows.anchor: من العرب من يقول هذا هنوك ورأيت هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem's عضوات supports deriving عضوي; another dialect treats عضة as hāʾ-final and says عضيهة, like شفة.
rows.anchor: عضيهة يجعلها من بنات الهاء بمنزلة شفة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl derives أخوي: the feminine tāʾ disappears in pluralization, exposing the root; nisba likewise removes tāʾ and restores the root consonant. Yūnus's أختي is not analogical.
rows.anchor: قلت أخوي هكذا ينبغي له أن يكون على القياس

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus instead says أختي, which Sībawayh explicitly calls non-analogical.
rows.anchor: وأما يونس فيقول أختي وليس بقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Diminutives do not restore a deleted root consonant: the remainder already fits a diminutive pattern, and the missing element is not an added suffix like tāʾ or feminine hāʾ.
rows.anchor: من قبل أن ما بقي إذا حقر يكون على مثال المحقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus ميت gives مييت from ميت after deletion of the middle radical, and هار gives هوير from هائر after deletion of hamza; both missing elements substitute for the middle radical.
rows.anchor: فمن ذلك قولك في ميت مييت وإنما الأصل ميت غير أنك حذفت العين

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus reports هويئر, a diminutive of the full هائر rather than truncated هار; Sībawayh says not to generalize such irregular forms without further Arabic evidence.
rows.anchor: وزعم يونس أن ناسا يقولون هويئر على مثال هويعر

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Yūnus reports Abū ʿAmr's forms مريء and يريء for مر and يري, with hamza as in مريع and the yāʾ of قاض; by this analysis he should also say مييت and أنيس.
rows.anchor: كان يقول في مر مريء مثل مريع وفي يري يريء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same no-restoration rule gives يضيع for a man called بيضع and خيير منك or شرير منك for خير منك and شر منك; augmentations are not restored.
rows.anchor: خيرا منك وشرا منك قلت
